section: Formation of Andhra Pradesh 1956 - Visalandhra, Gentlemen's Agreement
subsections: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology

accepted.s: Who founded the Visalandhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada on 26 November 1949?
accepted.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded at Vijayawada on 26 November 1949 under the leadership of Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–organisation association directly.

accepted.s: Which of the following works was written by P. Sundarayya in support of the Visalandhra idea?
accepted.x: P. Sundarayya wrote “Visalandhra Prajarajyam” in support of the Visalandhra concept.
accepted.tq: Apply the author–work matching approach.

accepted.s: Which of the following was the newspaper or party paper associated with the Communist advocacy of Visalandhra?
accepted.x: The Communist Party paper associated with the Visalandhra campaign was “Vishalandhra”.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact title from nearby political publications.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sri Sri — President of the Second Visalandhra Mahasabha
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao — Founder of Visalandhra Mahasabha
Marri Chenna Reddy — Strong supporter of Visalandhra throughout
accepted.x: Marri Chenna Reddy was an opponent of Visalandhra. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped political position among otherwise familiar associations.

accepted.s:
Consider the following persons:
1. Swami Ramananda Tirtha
2. Burgula Ramakrishna Rao
3. Mandumula Narsing Rao
4. Pandit Narendraji
Which of the above supported the Visalandhra movement?
accepted.x: All four—Swami Ramananda Tirtha, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, Mandumula Narsing Rao and Pandit Narendraji—supported Visalandhra.
accepted.tq: Test a complete supporter list through coded combinations.

accepted.s: The Socialists supported the Visalandhra idea through meetings held at which place in 1954?
accepted.x: The Socialists held meetings at Gudivada and Kurnool in 1954 in support of the Visalandhra idea.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired venues associated with a political group.

accepted.s: Which political organisation, in addition to the Socialists, supported the Visalandhra movement?
accepted.x: The Hindu Mahasabha was also listed among the supporters of Visalandhra.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation from a closely related political grouping.

accepted.s: The resolution supporting Visalandhra adopted by the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee was passed at Kurnool on:
accepted.x: The APCC adopted the relevant resolution at Kurnool on 30 September 1953.
accepted.tq: Use the date–event association and reject nearby movement dates.

accepted.s: Who changed his position from supporting Visalandhra to opposing it?
accepted.x: The poet Kaloji initially supported Visalandhra but later opposed it. K.V. Ranga Reddy is separately noted as having changed sides in the opposite political context.
accepted.tq: Separate two similar instances of changing political position.

accepted.s: Which of the following opponents of Visalandhra belonged to the Praja Socialist Party (PSP)?
accepted.x: Mahadev Singh of the PSP was an opponent of the Visalandhra proposal.
accepted.tq: Link the individual with the correct political organisation.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Founding of the Visalandhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada
B. First Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal
C. APCC resolution at Kurnool
D. Second Visalandhra Mahasabha at Hyderabad
accepted.x: The sequence is: founding at Vijayawada in November 1949, first Mahasabha at Warangal in February 1950, APCC resolution in September 1953, and second Mahasabha at Hyderabad in June 1954.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the middle events by year.

accepted.s: The first Visalandhra Mahasabha was held at Warangal on 12–13 February 1950 under the presidency of:
accepted.x: Hayagreevachari presided over the first Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal on 12–13 February 1950.
accepted.tq: Match the session venue and date with its presiding person.

accepted.s: Which of the following demands was associated with the first Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal?
o: Hyderabad should be the capital and Hyderabad State should be divided into three linguistic parts
Telangana should remain permanently separate from Andhra
Kurnool should be the permanent capital of Hyderabad State
accepted.x: The first Mahasabha called for Hyderabad as the capital and for Hyderabad State to be divided into three linguistic parts.
accepted.tq: Select the precise programme associated with a particular conference.

accepted.s: The slogan “Visalandhra nirmanam…” was associated with which leader at the Warangal meeting of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam gave the slogan “Visalandhra nirmanam…” at the Warangal meeting.
accepted.tq: Recall the speaker associated with a distinctive slogan.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the 1954 Visalandhra discussions is correct?
1. Some leaders argued for a separate Telangana.
2. Swami Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Visalandhra.
3. Ramananda Tirtha warned that a separate Telangana would be weak and vulnerable to suppression of democratic forces.
4. The Second Mahasabha was held at Warangal.
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Second Mahasabha was held at Hyderabad, not Warangal.
accepted.tq: Find the single wrong venue while retaining the substantive conference facts.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Socialists’ Kurnool meeting took place on 21–22 March 1954 and adopted a joint Andhra–Hyderabad resolution. The other dates and venues are mismatched.
accepted.tq: Start with the date–venue pair that is directly fixed in the chronology.

accepted.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh from 1964 to 1971?
accepted.x: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy served as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh from 1964 to 1971, with a second term beginning on 6 March 1967.
accepted.tq: Recall the tenure of the office-holder rather than only the name.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who served as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh immediately before the imposition of President’s Rule in January 1973?
accepted.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao served as Chief Minister from 1971 until President’s Rule began on 18 January 1973.
accepted.tq: Use the tenure boundary to distinguish adjacent Chief Ministers.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: President’s Rule in Andhra Pradesh during the early Chief Ministerial sequence lasted from:
accepted.x: President’s Rule was imposed from 18 January to 10 December 1973.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact start and end dates from other political transition periods.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Chief Minister succeeded Jalagam Vengala Rao in March 1978?
accepted.x: Marri Chenna Reddy succeeded Jalagam Vengala Rao on 6 March 1978.
accepted.tq: Test succession between two adjacent administrations.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the Chief Minister and tenure immediately preceding T. Anjaiah?
accepted.x: M. Chenna Reddy served from 6 March 1978 to 1980, immediately before T. Anjaiah, who began his tenure on 11 October 1980.
accepted.tq: Check the immediate predecessor and the adjoining tenure dates.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Chief Minister was in office when the Telugu Desam Party was founded on 29 March 1982?
accepted.x: The Telugu Desam Party was founded on 29 March 1982 during the tenure of Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy.
accepted.tq: Place the party’s founding date within the correct Chief Ministerial tenure.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh immediately before N.T. Rama Rao assumed office in January 1983?
accepted.x: Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy served from 20 September 1982 until January 1983, immediately before N.T. Rama Rao became Chief Minister.
accepted.tq: Use the last pre-1983 succession link to identify the correct office-holder.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Damodaram Sanjivayya?
1. He was the second Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
2. He became Chief Minister on 11 January 1960.
3. He later became President of the Indian National Congress.
4. He was never defeated in an election.
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect; the claim that Damodaram Sanjivayya was never defeated in an election is the false statement.
accepted.tq: Identify the incorrect biographical claim among several true details.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Chief Minister had the shortest tenure in the listed history of Andhra Pradesh, serving for 31 days in August–September 1984?
accepted.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao had the shortest tenure, lasting 31 days from 16 August to 16 September 1984.
accepted.tq: Match the exceptional duration with the correct office-holder.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who held the longest continuous tenure as Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh during 1995–2004?
accepted.x: N. Chandrababu Naidu had the longest continuous tenure as Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh, from 1995 to 2004.
accepted.tq: Compare the durations rather than merely recalling the sequence of office-holders.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the early political history of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. All Chief Ministers up to January 1983 belonged to the Congress.
2. N.T. Rama Rao was the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
3. Congress rule continued uninterrupted from 1956 until 1983.
4. The first non-Congress Chief Minister was Nadendla Bhaskara Rao.
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because N.T. Rama Rao, not Nadendla Bhaskara Rao, was the first non-Congress Chief Minister.
accepted.tq: Reject the swapped-person trap in a political succession statement.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which group of four Chief Ministers represents the successive administrations through which Congress changed four Chief Ministers in four years before the rise of the Telugu Desam Party?
o: M. Chenna Reddy, T. Anjaiah, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy
Jalagam Vengala Rao, P.V. Narasimha Rao, M. Chenna Reddy and N.T. Rama Rao
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy, P.V. Narasimha Rao, T. Anjaiah and N.T. Rama Rao
M. Chenna Reddy, Nadendla Bhaskara Rao, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy
accepted.x: The four Congress Chief Ministers were M. Chenna Reddy, T. Anjaiah, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy. Their rapid succession contributed to political fatigue before the TDP emerged.
accepted.tq: Select the complete and correctly ordered succession set.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Chief Ministers in chronological order of assuming office:
A. Jalagam Vengala Rao
B. M. Chenna Reddy
C. T. Anjaiah
D. Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy
accepted.x: Jalagam Vengala Rao assumed office in 1973, followed by M. Chenna Reddy in 1978, T. Anjaiah in 1980 and Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy in February 1982.
accepted.tq: Arrange the administrations using their tenure years and transition dates.
accepted.sec: Chief Ministers of early Andhra Pradesh - chronology  [APPSC]
